name: St Isaac's Cathedral
_about: ST ISAAC'S CATHEDRAL, St Petersburg (Montferrand, 1818-58), from its ground plan, OSM and the cross-section: the grey marble body on its granite podium, a giant Corinthian order round it; four porticoes of red granite monoliths (north and south of sixteen, east and west of eight) under pediments with their bronze reliefs and apostles; four corner towers, the north-west and south-east ones holding spiral stairs to the flat roof, each under a square belfry with a small gilded dome; the round stylobate to the colonnade walk at 43 m (a flight from the roof), the drum ringed by 24 columns with Hermann's angels on its balustrade, the attic, the gilded dome and its lantern, the cross at 101.5 m. Inside: three naves under barrel vaults crossed by the north-south arm, the dome on pendentives over the crossing, the iconostasis with its malachite and lapis columns, the sanctuary with the stained-glass Resurrection.

podium._about: the granite podium the church stands on: its floor, and the floors of the north and south porches between the corner towers

body._about: the body in grey Ruskeala marble: a giant Corinthian order of pilasters through the two storeys of windows -- the lower under pediments, the upper under cornices -- its entablature at the porticoes', the attic over it to the roof; the great doors behind the west, north and south porticoes, the altar window east

aedicules south._about: the aedicules round the end windows of the flanks: two columns, an entablature

pier line south._about: the pier line between the central nave and the side nave: the great arch round the crossing, arches either side, a door into the chapel at the east end

crossing wall west._about: the crossing's west and east sides: the great arch into the nave, arches into the side naves

west bay wall._about: between the west bay (the vestibule behind the great west door) and the nave: a wide arch, a smaller one into each side nave

sanctuary wall._about: the wall behind the iconostasis: the sanctuary's great arch, a door into each chapel either side of it

nave vault west arm._about: the central nave's barrel vaults, west and east of the crossing, wall to wall

arm vaults._about: the north-south arm's vaults, from the crossing to the north and south doors

pendentives._about: the pendentives over the crossing, and the roof round the drum's foot

roof ends._about: the flat roof, walked on: west and east of the crossing

interior._about: the church's space, from its floor to the vaults' crowns (to the walls' middles)

solea._about: the solea: the raised step before the iconostasis

iconostasis._about: the iconostasis: its screen of icons in three tiers, the royal doors in the middle, the deacons' doors either side

iconostasis malachite._about: the six malachite columns (9.66 m) of the iconostasis, gilt bases and capitals

iconostasis lapis._about: the two smaller lapis-lazuli columns beside the royal doors

iconostasis cornice._about: the gilt entablature over the iconostasis columns

altar._about: the altar table in the sanctuary

tower northeast._about: a corner tower: its order and windows like the body's, a door from the porch at its foot

tower floor northeast._about: the tower's floor at the roof's level

stair northwest._about: the spiral stair in the tower's outer corner, from the porch up to the roof's level, its floor round the head and the door onto the roof walk

stair southeast._about: the spiral stair in the tower's outer corner, from the porch up to the roof's level, its floor round the head and the door onto the roof walk

tower floor southwest._about: the tower's floor at the roof's level

tower heads._about: the cornice slab over each tower: the belfry's floor

belfry cores._about: the belfry: a square core, an arch on every side for the bells

belfry columns 0._about: the belfries' columns: two at each face, paired at the corners

belfry cornices._about: the cornice round the belfry's head

belfry pediments._about: the crossed pediments, one over each face

belfry domes._about: on each belfry a small gilded dome on its drum, its lantern and cross

portico south._about: an octastyle portico of red granite monoliths (17 m, Corinthian, bronze capitals) under its pediment and bronze relief

portico north._about: an octastyle portico of red granite monoliths (17 m, Corinthian, bronze capitals) under its pediment and bronze relief

portico west._about: an octastyle portico of red granite monoliths (17 m, Corinthian, bronze capitals) under its pediment and bronze relief

portico east._about: an octastyle portico of red granite monoliths (17 m, Corinthian, bronze capitals) under its pediment and bronze relief

portico south rows._about: the two rows of four columns behind the front row's first, third, sixth and eighth

steps south._about: the portico's nine granite steps, on three sides

portico north rows._about: the two rows of four columns behind the front row's first, third, sixth and eighth

steps north._about: the portico's nine granite steps, on three sides

stylobate._about: the round base of the dome over the roof: its top, round the drum, is the colonnade walk visitors climb to

dome well._about: the church's space on up through the stylobate to the drum's

colonnade stair._about: the flight from the roof walk up to the colonnade walk, on the east axis, stone parapets either side (iron ones read as two black strokes over the roof)

dome._about: the drum with its 12 windows and its peristyle of 24 granite columns, the windowed attic over them, the gilded dome with its ribs, the lantern and the cross

balustrade plinths._about: the balustrades' plinths, every run on the building (neoclassical.Balusters: the preferred L2 balustrade)
